summary: Burevestnik Airport (BVV/UHSB) is a small regional airport serving Kurilsk, the administrative center of Iturup Island in the Kuril Islands archipelago of Russia's Far East. It provides a vital air link between this remote volcanic island and mainland Russia, primarily handling short-haul propeller flights. The airport's location amid rugged terrain near active volcanoes makes it a distinctive gateway for visitors to one of the world's most isolated inhabited regions.
faqs:
Q: What is the nearest city to Burevestnik Airport?
A: The airport is located just outside Kurilsk, the main town and administrative center of Iturup Island in the Kuril Islands chain.

Q: How do you travel from Burevestnik Airport to Kurilsk town center?
A: The town is only a short drive from the airport, typically reached by taxi or pre-arranged transport. Roads on the island are limited, so transfers are usually arranged in advance.

Q: Is Burevestnik Airport open year-round?
A: Operations can be affected by the region's harsh weather, including heavy snow in winter and frequent fog. Travelers should expect potential schedule changes during severe conditions.

Q: Are there international flights from Burevestnik?
A: No, the airport primarily handles domestic flights within Russia, mainly connecting to Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk and other Far Eastern cities.
transport_tips: Getting to and from Burevestnik Airport requires advance planning, as public transportation on Iturup Island is very limited. Most travelers arrange taxi or hotel pickup in advance, and road conditions can be challenging due to the island's volcanic terrain and weather. Renting a vehicle locally is uncommon, so coordinated transfers are the most reliable option.
local_tip: If you have time between flights, ask locals about the nearby White Rocks (Belye Skaly) volcanic formations and the hot springs on the island—these geothermal sites are part of what makes Iturup geologically fascinating and are a favorite among returning visitors.
